doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Early drums, photos and the Laine home
title: First band on the air and undated photos
summary: Mrs. Laine says a band with Alfred Laine, Cousins and Marlowe was the first to play over the radio; the undated photos have faded.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You see, this band, that's the first band that ever played on the air, over the air. W-O-W-L. You can hardly see them anymore. Who was the man? Alfred Lane. Alfred Lane, he had that, and Jimmy Cousins and Marlowe and Bud Lawyer-Kaner was with him.
Yeah, what play? Is this the same Marlowe that helped Nick LaRocca learn his...

No, that's his brother. That's his brother. This fellow plays trombone, but the other, his brother played cornet, yeah. Manuel. Yeah. I had some of them pictures. I believe they're wrapped up. They're not... Yeah, that's the first band that ever played over the air.
Yeah, over the air. Say what that was about what... This is Johnny Root.
No, you can't read the date.
That's what she done wrong. She never dates these things. They should date them.
The ones I had was all dated.
Is that dated? It was dated, but I guess... That's so long.
